title: A Document Update in one Process can deterministically compel the initiation of another Process
content:
A.2.2.2.1.1.2 defines Document Update Triggers as "a type of gating condition that automatically or deterministically compels initiation of a Process in response to a specific Core Atlas or Agent Artifact Document Update in a previous Process Definition," and makes the obligation hard: "Once the specified Atlas or Artifact Document Update occurs (and assuming any specified Dependencies are also met), the Process **must** be initiated."

A.2.2.2.4 supplies the other half of the link from the producing side: a Required Output "can serve as a 'trigger' that deterministically compels another Process Definition to be initiated by a system or actor," with a `Trigger - Process` field naming the Process it initiates.

Together these turn the Primitive set into a **state machine over documents**. Processes do not call each other; they write documents, and document writes fire the next Process. The mediating artifact is the Atlas itself, which means every transition in the machine is a governance-visible record rather than an opaque internal message.

Two consequences follow. First, coupling is by data, not by procedure, so a Process need not know who consumes its output. Second, because initiation is mandatory rather than permissive, an incorrect Required Output can compel a downstream Process that nobody intended — the chain has no discretionary checkpoint unless a Dependency (A.2.2.2.1.2) supplies one.
description: Document Update Triggers plus the Required Outputs `Trigger - Process` link chain Primitive Processes into a state machine whose transitions are Atlas and Artifact document changes.
